column3: DSP nanoparticles for treating nitrogen mustard induced corneal injury
column4: PROJECT NARRATIVEThe goal of this project is to evaluate a new method by the subconjunctival injection of DSP nanoparticles fortreating nitrogen mustard (NM)-induced corneal injury. Therapeutic interventions to treat NM-induced ocularinjury has not been identified yet which highlights the need to develop new treatment options for vesicants-induced corneal injury. The sustained releasing DSP-PLA-NP could be effective in preventing corneal NVcorneal ulceration corneal opacity suppressing inflammatory and angiogenic markers after NM exposure.

column3: Developing next generation synthetic nucleic acid analogous for sickle cell disease gene editing
column4: Project NarrativePNAs are synthetic pieces of DNA that can bind to the chromosomes of cells in a targeted manner and stimulaterecombination of the target site with single-stranded donor DNAs to produce gene editing with extremely low offtarget effects compared to other approaches. We will test the novel PNAs for correction of a sickle cell-associatedmutation in the -globin gene in blood stem cells using nanoparticle-mediated delivery via IV administration inmice. We expect this work to yield potent PNAs and nanoparticle based approach to achieve curative geneediting for sickle cell disease.

column3: Forskolin-enhanced microfracture to regenerate hyaline cartilage in chondral defect
column4: Microfracture (MFx) a procedure creating small fractures in the subchondral bone is often considered as thefirstline procedure to treat cartilage injury. However neotissue in the defect site post-MFx is ultimatelyremodeled into fibrocartilage predisposing the repair site to premature degeneration. By repurposing the biosafeforskolin the next generation of MFx developed here would provide a minimally invasive and cost-affordableprocedure to achieve robust and long-term chondral defect repair.

column3: Therapeutic miRNA Modulation of Hepatocellular Carcinoma Using Ultrasound Guided Drug Delivery
column4: NarrativeTherapeutic options for patients with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) are limited particularly for those resistantto cytotoxic chemotherapeutics such as doxorubicin. Here we explore a novel genetic reprogramming approachtowards successfully treating HCC using a combination of microRNAs and an image-guided ultrasound andmicrobubble delivery platform which resensitizes HCC to doxorubicin. Effective therapeutic miRNA modulationmay fulfill the current therapeutic void for patients with advanced HCC and/or poor hepatic reserve and thisapproach can be readily adapted to other cancer types as well.

column4: Project NarrativePNAs are synthetic pieces of DNA that can bind to the chromosomes of cells in a targeted manner and stimulaterecombination of the target site with single-stranded donor DNAs to produce gene editing with extremely low offtarget effects compared to other approaches. column3: 3D Passive Cavitation Imaging-Guided Therapeutic Delivery of MicroRNA into Cancer
column4: PUBLIC HEALTH RELEVANCE:  New approaches to treating hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) are critically needed as therapeutic options are very limited and recurrence is common. Here we explore a novel genetic reprogramming approach to effectively treating HCC with reduced recurrence risk by delivering therapeutic microRNAs using an image- guided ultrasound and microbubble facilitated drug delivery platform. Guided by a roadmap predicting the treatment outcomes in real-time this approach allows adjustment and optimization of therapeutic delivery into the entire tumor thereby reducing the risk of recurrence from inappropriately treated regions.

column3: Nanoparticles for Immune Tolerance to FVIII
column4: PUBLIC HEALTH RELEVANCE: Hemophilia A is a life-threatening blood clotting disorder caused by mutations in factor VIII a clotting factor. The current therapy for this disorder is to administer functional factor VIII intravenously but a significant number of patients produce antibodies to the treatment making it ineffective. Our goal is to develop and translate novel therapeutic protocols to prevent and reverse this undesirable antibody formation by using immune modulatory nanoparticles developed by Selecta to induce tolerance to therapeutic factor VIII.
